newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Asian Gold - Traders eye gold in Aussie dollars.
newsitem.headline: Asian Gold - Traders eye gold in Aussie dollars.

text.p: Gold traders in Asia said on Friday they were keeping an eye on currency markets, particularly the Australian dollar, but physical demand remained limp.
"We still really have to watch the currencies for any impetus into the market," said one dealer.
Australian producers were not doing much selling, with the the gold price at its current levels, and if anything, there was some buying back in the markets, the dealer said.
"The main news for Aussie producers is they're still nervous, if (the spot price) collapses, what could happen to their future hedging," another dealer said.
Gold in Australian dollars was trading at $434.16 per ounce at 0603 GMT, near historic lows.

"People want to know what the overall effect on the Australian producers will be, will they buy back their hedges or whether you'll get panicking by people who havn't hedged earlier," a senior precious metals dealer said.
In the options markets, volatilities for gold in Australian dollars were higher than for US dollar gold, an options trader said.
"Whereas at-the-money (gold in) U.S. dollars is about 9.6 percent in the one month, at-the-money gold Aussie is around about 11 percent. There is a large premium," he said.
The options markets were also bearishly looking for downside plays with U.S. banks heard buying puts and selling calls.
Spot trading in Asia on Friday remained quiet, with Hong Kong midday gold unchanged from its opening price of US$340.20/70 per ounce.
"The funds are not there and neither are the producers. Volatility is absent. Prices are going to be in a tight range, although we might see fresh lows again," a Singapore dealer said.
Traders said the lethargic mood was compounded by China's three-day holiday celebrating the May 1 Labour day.
Some dealers said that spot gold saw good activity at the upper and lower ends of the range, keeping it trapped between $338 and $341 per ounce.

"Whenever there is some buying from dealers and funds, people cover their shorts and the market goes up close to $341, then selling comes in and the market gets lower," a senior dealer at a Hong Kong bullion firm said.
Prices would probably remain glued in a range between $338 to $343 an ounce in coming days with a test of the downside over the next few weeks seen likely, Singapore dealers said.

Physical demand was said to be average with a solid break through ranges needed to spark interest, gold traders said. They noted, however, that any break in the current range would be short-lived because of soft interest in gold.
"We haven't received inquiries for gold bars the last few days," a Singapore bank trader said, adding consumer demand around the region was quiet.
Traders said demand paled in comparison to the robust buying seen in February just before the Lunar New Year.
Hong Kong traders agreed, noting that buyers had stocked up when gold last hit $340 per ounce and now were even more price sensitive.
Singapore premiums over spot London prices were slightly easier at around 85-110 U.S. cents an ounce, against last week's 90-120 cents.
-- Hong Kong Newsroom (852) 2843 6358
-- Rene Pastor in Singapore (65) 8703305)
